Inept

/in-EPT/ — stress on EPT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is inept lacks the skill or ability needed to do something well, so their attempts usually fail.

His inept attempt at whistling sounded like a leaking balloon.

Worked Example

The new intern's inept handling of the database corrupted three months of financial records.

In (not) + aptus (fitted, suited) = not fitted for the task. The intern lacked the skill to manage the system. Inept is more precise than 'careless' because it names the fundamental lack of capability, not just a one-time mistake.

How Inept Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

incompetent

incompetent: lacking the ability to succeed

unskilled

unskilled: without the training the task needs

bungling

bungling: botching attempts through fumbling execution

Antonyms

adept

adept: highly skilled — inept's twin by construction

competent

competent: fully able to do the job properly

How Strong Is It? — clumsy → unskilled → bumbling → inept

clumsy vs. inept

clumsy vs. inept: A clumsy first attempt just needs more practice, but an inept attempt fails because the basic skill isn't there.

unskilled vs. inept

unskilled vs. inept: An unskilled worker simply hasn't been trained yet; an inept worker keeps failing even after the training.

bumbling vs. inept

bumbling vs. inept: A bumbling effort stumbles here and there, while an inept effort goes wrong from start to finish.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not (Latin)

Root — -ept

Root — -ept: fitted, suited (from Latin aptus) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: In- (not) + Latin aptus (fitted, suited) = not suited to the task, so attempts keep failing. Its skilled twin adept grew from the very same root — inept and adept are opposites by construction.

Use the root in a new word: aptitude

Use the root in a new word: aptitude: Her aptitude for numbers showed the first time she balanced the club's budget in minutes.

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for inept when someone fundamentally lacks the skill or ability for a task—not just making a one-time mistake, but demonstrating deep incompetence. It works equally well in casual contexts ('an inept dancer') and formal writing.
